item.title: [UPDATED] How to set a Screen Time passcode on an iPhone or iPad
item.description:
You can create a Screen Time passcode to ensure the settings you choose for your child's device or your own device remain in place. That means the passcode must be entered before you can change any Screen Time settings. When a Screen Time passcode is enabled for a child's device, you'll receive a notification any time the passcode is used on their device.

11 added · 13 removed

-With a Screen Time passcode, you can ensure the settings you choose for your child's device remain in place. That means the passcode must be entered before changing Screen Time settings. When a Screen Time passcode is enabled for a child's device, you receive a notification any time it's used on your child's device.
+You can create a Screen Time passcode to ensure the settings you choose for your child's device or your own device remain in place. That means the passcode must be entered before you can change any Screen Time settings. When a Screen Time passcode is enabled for a child's device, you'll receive a notification any time the passcode is used on their device.
-A Screen Time passcode isn’t the same as the passcode you use to unlock your device. It’s important to keep track of your Screen Time passcode because you need it to change the Screen Time settings for your device or a child’s device. You can change or remove a Screen Time passcode at any time.
+A Screen Time passcode isn’t the same as the passcode you use to unlock your device or a child's device. It’s important to keep track of your Screen Time passcode because you need it to change the Screen Time settings for your device or a child’s device. You can change or remove a Screen Time passcode at any time.
-If you use [Family Sharing](https://support.apple.com/108380) to manage a child’s Apple Account, the Family organizer needs to set the child's Screen Time passcode on their own device, not the child's device.
+If you use [Family Sharing](https://support.apple.com/108380) to manage a child’s Apple Account, the Family Sharing organizer or a parent/guardian needs to set the child's Screen Time passcode on their own device, not the child's device.

item.title: [UPDATED] If you're asked to confirm that you’re an adult
item.description:
When creating a new Apple Account or using Apple services, you might see a prompt to confirm that you're an adult. This is required by law in some states, countries and regions.

15 added · 9 removed

-When creating a new Apple Account or using Apple services, you might see a prompt to confirm that you’re an adult. This is required by law in some countries and regions.
+When creating a new Apple Account or using Apple services, you might see a prompt to confirm that you're an adult. This is required by law in some states, countries and regions.
-[Learn more about age requirements for managing an Apple Account by country or region](https://support.apple.com/125666)
+[Learn more about age requirements for managing an Apple Account by country or region](https://support.apple.com/en-us/125666)
-- Use a credit card — You can add a credit card that belongs to you to your Apple Account to confirm that you’re an adult. If you use a credit card, you have the option to [add it as a payment method for your Apple Account](https://support.apple.com/118429) . If you don’t add it as a payment method, your credit card isn’t stored. Debit cards aren't eligible.
+- Use a credit card — You can add a credit card that belongs to you to your Apple Account to confirm that you're an adult. If you use a credit card, you have the option to [add it as a payment method for your Apple Account](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118429) . If you don't add it as a payment method, your credit card isn’t stored. Debit cards aren't eligible.
-- Scan your ID — You can scan your passport (available in Singapore, the UK, and Texas in the United States)*, driver's license or government-issued ID to confirm that you're an adult. To help scan your ID successfully, make sure that you're in a well-lit place (indoors works best). Place your ID against a neutral background and avoid glare. Make sure that the image of your ID is clear and in focus before submitting. Apple and its service providers use the image of your ID to confirm you’re an adult and prevent fraud. The image of your ID is kept for a short period of time to complete this process, after which it's deleted.

item.title: [UPDATED] Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency modes for AirPods
item.description:
You can switch between Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency listening modes on your AirPods 4 and later, AirPods Pro, and AirPods Max, depending on how much of your surroundings you want to hear. You can also turn off listening modes.

23 added · 21 removed

-You can switch between Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency listening modes on your AirPods Pro and AirPods Max, depending on how much of your surroundings you want to hear. You can also turn off listening modes.
+You can switch between Active Noise Cancellation and Transparency listening modes on your AirPods 4 and later, AirPods Pro, and AirPods Max, depending on how much of your surroundings you want to hear. You can also turn off listening modes.
-With Active Noise Cancellation, an outward-facing microphone or microphones detect external sounds, which your AirPods 4 (ANC), AirPods Pro 1, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Max 1, and AirPods Max 2 then counter with anti-noise, canceling the external sounds before you hear them. An inward-facing microphone listens inside your ear for unwanted internal sounds, which your AirPods also counter with anti-noise.
+With Active Noise Cancellation, an outward-facing microphone or microphones detect external sounds, which your AirPods 4 (ANC), AirPods 5 (both models), AirPods Pro 1, AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Max 1, and AirPods Max 2 then counter with anti-noise, canceling the external sounds before you hear them. An inward-facing microphone listens inside your ear for unwanted internal sounds, which your AirPods also counter with anti-noise.
-If you have AirPods 4 (ANC), AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, or AirPods Max 2 and the [latest version of iOS or iPadOS](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118575) , you can also use [Adaptive Audio](https://support.apple.com/en-us/104979) , which adjusts the noise cancellation for you in response to and based on your surroundings.
